surfaceForm: It is the principal anchor of NIS2~Art.~21(2)(h) (cryptography policies and procedures)
proposedGenericDecision: NIS2 is an EU directive requiring national transposition; an EU-jurisdiction assumption is embedded by anchoring obligations to the directive article rather than to whatever applicable cybersecurity-law regime governs the adopting institution. Present as the EU exemplar of an applicable sector cybersecurity duty, with a hook for the local transposing/equivalent instrument.
suggestedLocalizationVariable: applicableCyberSecurityLaw (default: "NIS2 Directive Art. 21(2)(h) and its national transposition")
rationale: NIS2 binds only EU/EEA entities and only through national transposing law; a non-EU institution would map this duty onto a different instrument. The article reference is correct but jurisdiction-bound and assumes an unnamed EU member-state transposition context.

proposedGenericDecision: GDPR is an EU regulation; presenting it as the sole data-protection anchor assumes an EU data-protection regime. Frame as the EU exemplar of an applicable data-protection encryption duty, with a localization hook for the governing data-protection law (e.g., UK GDPR, FADP, state privacy law).
rationale: GDPR applies under the EU territorial/extraterritorial scope; an institution-agnostic suite serving non-EU adopters needs the encryption-of-personal-data duty expressed against the locally governing instrument. The specific clause is accurate but jurisdiction-bound.

surfaceForm: It is also the operational counterpart of eIDAS~2 trust services (qualified electronic signatures, seals and time stamps, when the institution provides them)
proposedGenericDecision: eIDAS 2 is an EU trust-services regulation; 'qualified' signature/seal/timestamp is an EU-specific legal category. Generalize to 'trust services under the applicable trust-services regime', keeping eIDAS 2 as the EU exemplar, since the 'when the institution provides them' guard already softens applicability.
rationale: The 'qualified' tier and eIDAS framework are EU-jurisdiction constructs; a generic adopter outside the EU has different (or no) qualified-trust-service categories. The conditional clause limits but does not remove the EU assumption.

surfaceForm: plus institutional governance for the CA hierarchy (root rotation, intermediate rotation, revocation procedures)
proposedGenericDecision: 'institutional governance' is already role-based and generic; no specific governance body (rectorate / board of governors) is named. Keep as-is.
rationale: Verified by reading: the chapter consistently uses the role placeholder 'the institution' and 'institutional governance' with no rectorate/board-of-governors shape assumed. Flagged only to record that governance was checked and found already generic.

surfaceForm: would typically require a small dedicated team --- indicatively one to two engineers shared with the security and identity teams
proposedGenericDecision: An FTE estimate (one-to-two engineers) is a sizing assumption that scales with institution size and labour-market context, even though no currency/jurisdiction is attached. It is already hedged ('indicatively', 'typically'). Keep but mark as a sizing constant that an instantiation may parameterize per scale.
suggestedLocalizationVariable: cryptoServicesFteEstimate (optional default: "1-2 engineers shared with security/identity")
rationale: Per the minimal-necessary-set principle the functional set is size-invariant while instantiation scales; the FTE figure is an instantiation-scale hint, already heavily hedged and not bound to any named jurisdiction or EUR amount, so it is closer to keep than parameterize.

proposedGenericDecision: TAC is an internal suite term (project-coined audit schema), not an institution name; cross-references and the TAC acronym are suite-internal and remain valid in any adopting instance. Keep.
rationale: Checked for an implicit UL-term macro expansion: TAC and \trchap targets are suite-internal architecture vocabulary, not institution-specific. Recorded to show macros were inspected.
